glosses: as it is; still (in that state)
patterns.usage_note: Freezes a state: whatever the preceding た-form, noun + の, or い-adjective describes stays in force while the main clause happens, often with a hint that it should not have. Hence 靴を履いたまま, 昔のまま, 冷たいまま. まんま is the casual spoken variant; the stiff, literary near-synonym たなり / だなり says much the same thing but is far rarer and confined to writing.

examples.ruby: 靴[くつ]を履[は]いたまんま部屋[へや]に上[あ]がっちゃだめだよ。
examples.english: You can't come up into the room with your shoes still on.

examples.ruby: 祖母[そぼ]の家[いえ]の台所[だいどころ]は、昔[むかし]のまんまだった。
examples.english: The kitchen in my grandmother's house was exactly as it had always been.

examples.ruby: このスープ、冷[つめ]たいまんまでも十分[じゅうぶん]おいしいよ。
examples.english: This soup tastes plenty good even cold.

glosses: and stayed that way ever since
patterns.usage_note: A stiff, literary equivalent of 〜たまま: someone does something once and the resulting state simply persists, usually with the implication that the expected follow-up never came. Unlike まま it attaches to a past verb only. It attaches where た attaches, so nasal and ガ-row godan verbs voice it to だなり (脱いだなり, 読んだなり). It belongs to written narration; in speech people say まま. Keep it apart from the 〜なり that follows a dictionary form and means "the instant that".

examples.ruby: 老人[ろうじん]は窓辺[まどべ]に座[すわ]ったなり、一言[ひとこと]も口[くち]をきかなかった。
examples.english: The old man sat down by the window and did not speak a single word after that.

examples.ruby: 客[きゃく]は帽子[ぼうし]を脱[ぬ]いだなり、玄関[げんかん]に立[た]ち尽[つ]くしていた。
examples.english: The visitor took off his hat and then just stood there in the entryway.

examples.ruby: 祖父[そふ]は一礼[いちれい]したなり、二度[にど]と振[ふ]り返[かえ]らなかった。
examples.english: My grandfather gave a single bow and never looked back again.
